Zorvio Analytical Figures & Visual Gallery

All 16 empirical charts generated by the exploratory data analysis notebooks (outputs/figures/), self-contained with takeaways and findings traceability.

F001 & F002 (Q1 & Q2)

Figure 1: Monthly Churn Trend (Jan 2024 – Dec 2025)

Core Takeaway: Baseline voluntary churn averages 5.52%. An acute spike to 11.18% occurred in October 2025 following a major infrastructure outage, recovering within 60 days.

F009 (Q7)

Figure 3: Raw Acquisition Channel Churn Ranking

Core Takeaway: App Store shows the highest raw churn (58.86%), but cross-stratification reveals this is confounded by an 82.1% Starter plan concentration.

F005 (Q3)

Figure 2: Lifetime Churn Rate by Plan Tier

Core Takeaway: Raw cumulative churn rates are virtually identical across tiers (Starter: 56.70%, Scale: 56.71%, Growth: 56.38%). Underlying hazard is ~7.4% per customer-month.

F006 (Q3)

Figure 4: Multidimensional Customer Segmentation

Core Takeaway: Annual billing contracts show substantially lower churn hazard across all company sizes and city tiers (commitment effect).

F009 (Q7)

Figure 5: Channel by Plan Stratification (Simpson's Paradox)

Core Takeaway: Controlling for plan tier eliminates channel variation (7.0%–8.1% per customer-month), proving App Store traffic is not intrinsically defective.

F003 & F004 (Q4)

Figure 6: Churn Hazard by Tenure Bucket

Core Takeaway: Steep early mortality cliff: Month 0–3 hazard is ~46% per customer-month, dropping 20x to ~2% beyond Month 13.

F003 (Q3)

Figure 7: Triangular Cohort Retention Matrix Heatmap

Core Takeaway: Tracks 24 monthly cohorts across M1–M12. Average 6-month retention is 69.3%. Blank cells indicate unobserved future calendar months.

F007 (Q6)

Figure 8: Average Weekly Usage: Churned vs Retained Accounts

Core Takeaway: Accounts that eventually cancel show early session velocity decay and engagement drop-off 30 to 60 days prior to formal cancellation.

F008 (Q5)

Figure 10: Multi-User Collaboration Adoption Moat

Core Takeaway: Adopting team collaboration features is associated with half the churn hazard (12.37% vs 24.67%, RR = 1.99x; n=18,242 vs 3,563).

F007 (Q6)

Figure 9: Inactivity Signal & Prospective Churn Risk

Core Takeaway: Zero sessions in 30 days is associated with an 89.47% churn rate vs 14.05% for active users (RR = 6.37x). Flagged for n=95 sample size.

F010 & F012 (Q10)

Figure 11: Prospective Leading Indicator Relative Risk Ranking

Core Takeaway: Rank ordering of early behavioral warning signals evaluated out-of-time across 22 monthly rolling snapshots.

F011 (Q9)

Figure 13: Exposed MRR by Risk Tier

Core Takeaway: Exposed active revenue is concentrated in Medium and High risk accounts, providing operational routing for customer success teams.

F012 (Q11)

Figure 12: Rule-Based Risk Framework Monotonicity Validation

Core Takeaway: Prospective validation shows strict monotonic risk escalation: Low (12.41%) -> Medium (22.28%) -> High (68.46%) -> Critical (100.0%).

F010 (Q8)

Figure 14: Active MRR Concentration by Plan Tier

Core Takeaway: Scale accounts concentrate 41.2% of active MRR (INR 6.55M) despite comprising only 13.3% of active customer volume.

F011 (Q9)

Figure 15: Realized Churned MRR Losses Over Time

Core Takeaway: Cumulative INR 21.00M in recurring revenue permanently lost, with acute spikes during the infrastructure outage period.

F011 (Q9)

Figure 16: Three Distinct Measures of Revenue at Risk

Core Takeaway: Distinguishes Realized historical losses (INR 21.00M), Exposed portfolio MRR (INR 520K inst. / INR 3.84M tot.), and Expected loss (INR 411,712 with Wilson CI).
